heading: Why Ixmucané. Why GeoPower.
p1: In the Popol Vuh — the K'iche' Maya creation narrative, and one of Guatemala's own foundational texts — Ixmucané is the grandmother creator: a diviner who, with her counterpart Xpiyacoc, reads fate in maize kernels and casts the calendar itself. After failed attempts to shape people from mud and from wood, it's Ixmucané who grinds white and yellow maize into the dough that becomes the first true humans. She is patience, wisdom, and the long, careful work of bringing something real out of the earth's own materials.
p2: That's the same work we do, several thousand years and one discipline later — drawing power out of the earth itself, carefully, not quickly. GeoPower is the plain half of the name: geothermal, power, engineering. Ixmucané is the other half, a nod to the ground this company is built on, literally and otherwise.
